newsitem.title: Italy: Italian shares close slightly higher, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close slightly higher, led by banks.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Milan shares closed firmer helped by the higher trend in domestic bonds and the lira, while a rise in banking shares also gave support as the deadline for bids for Banco di Napoli drew ever closer, dealers said.

* BCI gained as it denied interest in the Naples bank while Ambroveneto also rose although it has not decided yet on whether to bid. Among other shares, STET suffered from profit takers after seeing strong rises on Monday and Tuesday after the release of merger plans with telephone company Telecom Italia.
* The all-share Mibtel index ended up 0.25 percent at 10,166 with the Mib30 index 0.2 percent firmer at 15,287.

* BCI's managing director Luigi Fausti said his bank had no plans for intervention regarding the Banco di Napoli, while Ambroveneto board member Gino Trombi said his bank had not yet made a decision over the Naples-based bank.

* These two northern Italian banks have been rumoured to be two most likely Italian banks to be interested in bidding for a stake in loss-making Banco di Napoli. Bids need to be sent to the Italian Treasury by November 18.
* BCI shares rose to a day's high of 2,930 lire before settling to close up 2.71 percent at 2,881 lire, while Ambroveneto ended up 4.89 percent at 3,365 lire.
* Dealers said a bid for Banco di Napoli could well be a costly exercise to bring the ailing bank back into profit.
* STET shares closed off 3.46 percent at 5,991 lire while Telecom Italia was up 1.56 percent at 3,383 lire and TIM closed off 0.09 percent at 3,492 lire.
* Olivetti continued to gain up 2.62 percent at 508.7 lire after announcing its net debt at end-September was little changed at 2.415 trillion lire after 2.39 trillion end-August.
* Fiat ended off 1.46 percent at 4,535 lire after it denied rumours of a sale or reorganisation at its biomedical unit Sorin and its majority-held chemicals and fibres company Snia Bpd.
